messages:
darya: quick spike idea: instead of tail-index/tombstone or full sidecar manifest, what about a tiny start-of-object micro-index (SOI) we prepend to safetensors bundles to make streaming and warmstart deterministic with one small head read?

sam: head-read vs tail-read tradeoffs? wondering about multipart and streaming semantics.

darya: rationale: head reads are generally supported and slightly cheaper when you already do a header parse. for headerless blobs the loader can range-read first 512 bytes, parse SOI that contains per-chunk offsets (compact), a small checksum, and a feature map (quantized layers list).

maria: curious what "compact" looks like. 512 bytes can carry what, offsets for like 8 chunks at 64-bit each is already 64 bytes, so we can do more metadata.

darya: proposed layout (example, packed binary TLV):
- magic(8) | version(1) | flags(1) | header_len(u16) | compressed_flag(1) | chunk_count(u8) | for i in chunk_count: chunk_offset_delta(u32) | chunk_size(u32) | quant_flag(u8) | reserved... | sha1(payload_summary 20)
Total target: <= 512 bytes. offsets are deltas to reduce size.

aj: offset deltas make sense for large models with many small chunks. but what about variable shard sizes and thousands of chunks? 512 bytes won't be enough.

darya: for extreme shardization (N>32), SOI contains a pointer to an expanded index stored at a well-known offset in the same object (e.g., immediate next block) or a sidecar. Loader fallback: if chunk_count==0 or pointer set -> go sidecar/index-first. We optimize for the common case: modest chunk counts for streaming-friendly shards.

rachel: security: head-read can be served during multi-part upload too. how do we avoid racing with in-progress uploads?

darya: pattern: ingest writes a zeroed SOI until finalization. finalization writes the real SOI atomically by a small overwrite of first 512 bytes (supported by many object stores if you use a two-step: upload final object then do a server-side rewrite). If provider doesn't support in-place small rewrites, we write final object to key and then rename/compose. Loader semantics: treat SOI as valid only if magic+version+sha check match. otherwise fallback to manifest.

sam: what does loader flow look like?

darya: loader pseudocode: 
```
head = range_read(object_key, 0, 511)
if head.magic == "SOI01" and verify_sha(head.summary):
  parse chunk table -> for each needed chunk -> range_read(chunk_offset, chunk_offset+size-1)
else if head.has_index_pointer:
  read_index_at(pointer) -> stream
else:
  index_first_fallback()
```

maria: telemetry please: head_hit, head_corrupt, head_latency, head_index_pointer_follow. Also count fallbacks to sidecar.

aj: perf: head read can be cached by edge CDN and is often <10ms in-region. tail reads sometimes miss cache and incur higher P95. Good point.

darya: migration: 1) loader accepts SOI or falls back. 2) new ingestion clients emit SOI. 3) background migration tool rewrites hot blobs with SOI. 4) deprecate sidecar requirement for new uploads.

sam: how about compressed objects? if object is gzipped we can't interpret offsets.

darya: define SOI only for raw (uncompressed) object variants. For compressed we store an uncompressed header region followed by a compressed payload with marker that points to sidecar. Alternatively, during ingest we can produce a separate uncompressed header object keyed alongside the blob (fast metadata fetch).
maria: edgecase: multi-range read amplification when many small chunks requested in parallel. Suggest grouping nearby chunks and requesting multi-range or single larger ranges.

darya: agreed — loader should coalesce ranges within a sliding window and use continuous reads when helpful. also provide a batch_range API in the runtime to reduce request count.

aj: provider differences: azure block blobs don’t support ranged writes; renames behave differently. add provider guide.

infra-bot: test-check: add head-corrupt and head-missing simulations to unit tests + integration with CDN cache knobs.

sam: sounds plausible. can you write an RFC that includes binary layout, fallbacks, migration CLI, and bench plan?

darya: yep i'll RFC it. will include example of delta-encoded offsets, pointer convention for expanded-index, and migration ordering.

maria: +1 to RFC. also call out telemetry quotas for head probes so we don't flood the catalog.

aj: +1 but add a note about eval reproducibility when loader uses SOI vs sidecar — ensure content-addressed verification before activation.

darya: good catch, will include activation checksum verification and optional tombstone signed metadata for enterprise mode.
